s.en: list section sizes and total size of binary files

o.en: Using one of these options, you can choose whether the output from GNU size resembles output from System V size (using -A, or --format=sysv), or Berkeley size (using -B, or --format=berkeley). The default is the one-line format similar to Berkeley's.

Using one of these options, you can control whether the size of each section is given in decimal (-d, or --radix=10); octal (-o, or --radix=8); or hexadecimal (-x, or --radix=16). In --radix=number, only the three values (8, 10, 16) are supported. The total size is always given in two radices;
Print total size of common symbols in each file. When using Berkeley or GNU format these are included in the bss size.
Show totals of all objects listed (Berkeley or GNU format mode only).
Specify that the object-code format for objfile is bfdname. This option may not be necessary; size can automatically recognize many formats.
Display the version number of size.
Ignored. This option is used by other versions of the size program, but it is not supported by the GNU Binutils version.
